chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"If a man falls ill from one Ramadan to the next, then recovers, then for every day he broke the fast, the ransom is food, and it is a mudd for each poor person."
He said, "And likewise in the expiation of the oath and the expiation of the zihar, a mudd, a mudd."
And if he recovered in between the two Ramadans, then he is only required to make up the fasting.
But if he neglected it while he was recovered, then upon him is the charity and the fasting together, for every day a mudd, when he finishes that Ramadan."

key_terms.فِدْيَةٌ: Ransom or compensation for missed worship
key_terms.كَفَّارَةُ اَلظِّهَارِ: Expiation for the Islamic declaration of separation (zihar)
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific unit of volume for food

ai.seo_question: What is the fidya for chronic illness lasting from one Ramadan to the next?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* distinguishes between chronic illness persisting across two Ramadans, which incurs only fidya (one mudd per day), and temporary illness where neglecting makeup fasts after recovery necessitates both fidya and qada. It further aligns the fidya rate with that of expiation for oaths and zihar, reflecting the juristic principle of consistency in compensation metrics within Shia fiqh.
